question: 102 men have enough food supplies for 30 weeks. Along with them, 78 more men join. For how many weeks will the food supplies last?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Men = 102, Final Men = 102 + 78 = 180.

Ratio of Men = 102 : 180 = 17 : 30.

Since time is inversely proportional to the number of men, Ratio of Time = 30 : 17.

30 units → 30 weeks, so 17 units → 17 weeks.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 weeks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = 102

Initial number of weeks (D₁) = 30

Final number of men (M₂) = 102 + 78 = 180

**Formula Used:**

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

 102 Men × 30 Weeks Total Food = 180 Men × ? Weeks Total Food M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Food = M₁ × D₁ = 102 × 30 = 3060 units

⇒ Total Food = M₂ × D₂

⇒ 3060 = 180 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 3060 ÷ 180

⇒ D₂ = 17

**∴ The correct answer is 17 weeks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

If M₁ men can do W₁ work in D₁ days, and M₂ men can do W₂ work in D₂ days, then (M₁ × D₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) ÷ W₂.

Inverse Proportion

When the total work or total food provision is constant, the time required is inversely proportional to the number of men consuming or working (Men ∝ 1 ÷ Time).

Direct Proportion

If the number of men is constant, the amount of work done or food consumed is directly proportional to the time taken (Work ∝ Time).
